problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.statement: Determine if a string is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring cases.
problems.understanding: Ignore spaces and punctuation; check if string equals its reverse.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Filter alphanumeric characters into a new string and reverse it.

problems.intuition: Use two pointers converging inward from left and right ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters in O(1) space.
problems.approach:
1. Initialize left = 0, right = len(s) - 1.
  2. Advance left while not s[left].isalnum().
  3. Decrement right while not s[right].isalnum().
  4. Compare lowercased characters. If match, move both pointers inward.

problems.title: Two Sum II — Input Array Is Sorted
problems.statement: Given a 1-indexed sorted array of integers numbers, find two numbers that add up to target.
problems.understanding: Array is already sorted in non-decreasing order.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Try every pair with two nested loops.

problems.intuition: Leverage sorted property: two pointers at ends. If sum < target, increment left; if sum > target, decrement right.
problems.approach:
1. Set left = 0, right = len(numbers) - 1.
  2. Compute total = numbers[left] + numbers[right].
  3. If total == target, return 1-based indices [left + 1, right + 1].
  4. If total < target, move left += 1. Else move right -= 1.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Sorted array + Target Sum → Two Pointers

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.statement: Find all unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j != k and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.
problems.understanding: Triplets must sum to zero and contain no duplicate triplets in output.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Triple nested loop + set of sorted tuples to eliminate duplicates.

problems.intuition: Sort array. Fix index i, then use two pointers left and right to solve Two Sum II for remainder. Skip duplicate values.
problems.approach:
1. Sort nums.
  2. Loop i from 0 to n-3. Skip if nums[i] == nums[i-1].
  3. Run Two Pointers on left = i+1, right = n-1.
  4. When match found, append triplet and advance both pointers past duplicate values.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.statement: Given an integer array height, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container containing the most water.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Check area between all pairs of vertical lines.

problems.intuition: Start with widest pointers (left=0, right=n-1). To potentially increase area as width shrinks, move the pointer pointing to the shorter line.
problems.approach:
1. Place left = 0, right = len(height) - 1.
  2. Compute area = (right - left) * min(height[left], height[right]).
  3. Update answer = max(answer, area).
  4. If height[left] < height[right], move left += 1; else right -= 1.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Shrinking width → Discard pointer with smaller height

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.statement: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: For every position, scan left and right to find maximum wall heights.

problems.intuition: Prefix/Suffix arrays give max left/right in O(n) space. Compress prefix/suffix into Two Pointers with running max variables for O(1) space.
problems.approach:
1. Maintain left = 0, right = n - 1, and running left_max, right_max.
  2. If height[left] <= height[right], update left_max or add left_max - height[left], then left += 1.
  3. Else, update right_max or add right_max - height[right], then right -= 1.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Prefix/Suffix information compressed into Two Pointers + running max state
